log.user:
Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

judgment_calls: INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS lists 'internal audit function', and the response's own CONFIDENCE_NOTES calls it 'inferred only from the reference to its June 2026 report'. I decided this is supported rather than a new Client fact. The notes say 'Internal audit reported in June 2026' and list 'two internal auditors' among attendees, so an internal audit function exists on the material's own terms. No scope, program or owner is asserted. A stricter scorer could read the self-described inference as a breach of Rule 1 and the incumbent-function guidance, and mark FAIL.
I treated 'run by Ingrid Solberg' as traceable because the notes say 'Ingrid runs the quality management system under ISO 9001'. The Rule 6 ownership concern does not arise here.
I treated the CONFIDENCE_NOTES entries as permitted notes on ambiguity, not as commentary outside the block.
score.reasoning: The output is one fenced block with all fields present, the halt is correctly not triggered, and the values trace to the discovery notes. The response avoided the likely traps: it assigned no owner to the ISMS, recorded no AI inventory as an incumbent control, and kept the 42001 aim as 'would like to start ... work' without calling it a certification commitment. The only borderline item is the 'internal audit function' entry. The material supports an internal audit body existing, so I scored it as met and flagged the dissent risk.
